faq.q: Why are leaves broad and flat?
faq.a: A broad leaf has a large surface area to absorb as much light as possible, and a thin leaf lets carbon dioxide reach the inner cells quickly by diffusion.
asks: Tell me about the broad flat blade

faq.a: The palisade layer is a row of tall, tightly packed cells near the top of the leaf. They contain the most chloroplasts, so most photosynthesis happens there.
asks: Tell me about the palisade layer

faq.a: Stomata are tiny pores, mostly on the underside of a leaf. They let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out. Each pore is opened and closed by two guard cells.
Veins contain xylem, which brings water and minerals from the roots, and phloem, which carries the sugar made in the leaf to the rest of the plant. They also help hold the leaf flat.

faq.q: Why are most stomata on the underside?
faq.a: The underside is shaded and cooler, so less water evaporates through the pores than it would on the sunny upper side.
asks: Why are stomata on the bottom of leaves?

facts: Most chloroplasts in a leaf are in the palisade mesophyll near the upper surface.
Each stoma is surrounded by two guard cells that open and close it.

quiz.say: What gas enters a leaf through the stomata for photosynthesis?
quiz.show: What gas enters a leaf through the stomata for photosynthesis?
quiz.why: Carbon dioxide diffuses in through the stomata and is used to make glucose.

wrong.0: Oxygen is made in photosynthesis and goes out of the leaf.
wrong.2: Plants do not take nitrogen gas in through their leaves for photosynthesis.

quiz.say: Why are palisade cells near the top of the leaf?
quiz.show: Why are palisade cells near the top of the leaf?
quiz.why: Light falls on the upper surface first, so cells full of chloroplasts there can use the most light.

wrong.1: Warmth is not the reason for their position.
wrong.2: The roots are far away underground.
